parameters.query:
-- Apply an inbound event (a booking, an approval decision, a customer reply) exactly
-- once, whatever the provider does with delivery.
--
-- The claim is keyed on the *provider's* identifier for the event, not on our receipt
-- of it, so a webhook delivered twice collapses to one application (edge case 11).
WITH args AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS a
),
d AS (
  SELECT a AS root, a->>'key' AS key, a->>'lead_id' AS lead_id, a->'lead_patch' AS patch
  FROM args
),
claimed AS (
  INSERT INTO idempotency_claim
    (key, effect_domain, entity_type, entity_id, occurrence, state, attempt, response, settled_at, stale_after)
  SELECT
    d.key,
    split_part(d.key, ':', 2),
    split_part(d.key, ':', 3),
    split_part(d.key, ':', 4),
    split_part(d.key, ':', 5),
    'succeeded', 1, d.root->'event', now(), now()
  FROM d
  WHERE d.key IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING key
),
-- Everything below is gated on winning the claim, so a redelivery changes nothing at
-- all rather than changing things slightly differently.
patched AS (
  UPDATE lead l SET
    status               = COALESCE(NULLIF(d.patch->>'status',''), l.status),
    approval_state       = COALESCE(NULLIF(d.patch->>'approval_state',''), l.approval_state),
    consent_status       = COALESCE(NULLIF(d.patch->>'consent_status',''), l.consent_status),
    consent_ts           = CASE WHEN d.patch ? 'consent_status' THEN now() ELSE l.consent_ts END,
    disposition          = COALESCE(NULLIF(d.patch->>'disposition',''), l.disposition),
    status_reason        = COALESCE(NULLIF(d.patch->>'status_reason',''), l.status_reason),
    last_sales_action_at = CASE WHEN d.patch ? 'sales_action' THEN now() ELSE l.last_sales_action_at END,
    version              = l.version + 1,
    updated_at           = now()
  FROM d
  WHERE l.lead_id = d.lead_id
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claimed)
    AND jsonb_typeof(d.patch) = 'object'
  RETURNING l.lead_id, l.owner_id, l.odoo_lead_id
),
approval_decided AS (
  UPDATE approval_request ar
  SET state      = d.root->>'approval_state',
      decided_at = now(),
      decided_by = NULLIF(d.root->>'decided_by',''),
      reason     = NULLIF(d.root->>'approval_reason','')
  FROM d
  WHERE ar.token = NULLIF(d.root->>'approval_token','')
    AND ar.state = 'pending'
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claimed)
  RETURNING ar.id, ar.lead_id
),
-- Stopping a sequence is two things: cancel what is queued, and re-check state at
-- dispatch. Both, because either alone leaves a window.
stopped AS (
  UPDATE work_queue w
  SET state = 'cancelled', updated_at = now(),
      last_error = jsonb_build_object('cancelled_by', d.root->>'workflow',
                                      'reason', d.root->>'cancel_reason')
  FROM d
  WHERE jsonb_typeof(d.root->'cancel_kinds') = 'array'
    AND w.lead_id = d.lead_id
    AND w.state = 'pending'
    AND w.kind IN (SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(d.root->'cancel_kinds'))
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claimed)
  RETURNING w.id
),
enqueued AS (
  INSERT INTO work_queue (kind, lead_id, payload, idempotency_key, run_after, max_attempts)
  SELECT q->>'kind', d.lead_id, COALESCE(q->'payload','{}'::jsonb), NULLIF(q->>'idempotency_key',''),
         now() + (COALESCE((q->>'delay_seconds')::numeric, 0) * interval '1 second'),
         COALESCE((q->>'max_attempts')::int, 5)
  FROM d, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(d.root->'enqueue','[]'::jsonb)) q
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claimed)
  RETURNING id
),
-- Consequences are audited only when the claim was won, so a redelivery never
-- writes a second "booking applied" that never happened.
audit AS (
  INSERT INTO event_log
    (lead_id, workflow, execution_id, step, event_type, decision, inputs, outputs, idempotency_key, severity)
  SELECT d.lead_id, d.root->>'workflow', d.root->>'execution_id',
         e->>'step', e->>'event_type', e->>'decision', e->'inputs', e->'outputs',
         d.key, COALESCE(NULLIF(e->>'severity',''), 'info')
  FROM d, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(d.root->'events','[]'::jsonb)) e
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claimed)
  RETURNING id
),
-- The delivery itself is always recorded, won or not. Knowing a provider sent the
-- same webhook three times is operationally useful, and it is the evidence that
-- suppression happened rather than the message never arriving.
delivery_log AS (
  INSERT INTO event_log
    (lead_id, workflow, execution_id, step, event_type, decision, inputs, outputs, idempotency_key, severity)
  SELECT d.lead_id, d.root->>'workflow', d.root->>'execution_id', 'inbound', 'webhook.delivered',
         CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claimed) THEN 'applied' ELSE 'duplicate_suppressed' END,
         jsonb_build_object('source', d.root->>'source', 'provider_event_id', d.root->>'provider_event_id'),
         jsonb_build_object('key', d.key),
         d.key,
         CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claimed) THEN 'info' ELSE 'warn' END
  FROM d
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM claimed)          AS applied,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM patched)          AS lead_patched,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM approval_decided) AS approval_decided,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM stopped)          AS work_cancelled,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM enqueued)         AS enqueued,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM audit)            AS audit_rows,
  (SELECT odoo_lead_id FROM patched)           AS odoo_lead_id,
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM delivery_log)     AS delivery_logged;
